prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website composition probe for an Effective HTML catalog page, 16:10 landscape.
Reference image role: preserve the exact Working Atlas identity only — near-black Ink field, warm bone paper, cobalt, lilac, green, pink and coral spot colors, bold compressed grotesk, thin black rules, subtle physical paper tooth, crisp HTML geometry and controlled asymmetry. Do not copy the existing landing composition.
Primary request: Design a complete catalog page using an EDITORIAL CATEGORY BANDS composition. Thin site navigation. A concise upper-left title reads exactly “Catalog”; beside it a dense irregular contact-sheet cluster previews several genuinely different artifact forms. Below, the catalog is organized into broad full-width horizontal bands for Exploration, Review, Design, Prototyping, Diagrams, Research, Reports, and Editors. Each band uses a different large flat printed-ink field and contains two or three staggered specimen sheets of unequal size, with a narrow label rail and compact actions to open HTML or switch between static and animated SVG. The first two bands should be visible in the composition so the scrolling rhythm is clear. Include a small search control and a source index, but let the artifacts lead. Add one thin bottom teaser for the Effective HTML skills.
Visible text: only “Effective HTML”, “Catalog”, “Exploration”, “Review”, “HTML”, “Static”, and “Animated” need be legible; other copy should appear as short indistinct lines.
Constraints: a real responsive website interface, not a poster, collage photo, or desk. No generic equal card grid, dashboard chrome, gradients, glass, glow, photographs, human hands, mascots, connector lines, fake 3D, or dense tiny prose. Flat matte and implementable with semantic HTML/CSS and real SVG previews.
